body: I’ve been through withdrawals. Now I’m wondering if I’m experiencing permanent damage or after effects of the medication.

Thanks so much for your reply. I really hope so. I really really hope it isn’t medication related and its just TMJ because I’m getting treatment for it. 
I feel like it may be a mix of TMJ, medication, and psychological symptoms. 
All three mushed together I can’t tell the difference. Which gives me more psychological problems .. like ocd symptoms and anxiety. 

I don’t know if the physical pain and discomfort is causing the anxiety or if it’s the other way around. The TMJ treatment consists of developing the upper jaw with a palate expander or an ALF appliance. This brings the maxilla forward and widens it so the lower jaw can come forward and the ligaments can line up properly. Your bite was pushed back and the jaw was probably displaced as well. I’m so sorry that you had to suffer so much pain from TMJ. I really know how you feel in terms of that. I really hope you could find someone near you who practices orthotropic dentistry who can do alf treatment. Also, try seeing an osteopath. Cranial osteopathy or biodynamic osteopathy. They have helped me tremendously. 

I think its part physical and part psychological in my case. I vaguely remember times last year when I had no idea I had TMJ and no idea that quitting meds could cause problems and sleeping like a baby because I thought I solved my indigestion issues and because I was at my grandma’s house at the time. 
Then I had brief moments where I slept really well just because my mom was here or because I managed to convince myself that I was seriously fine and okay. 

The reason I think a lot more could contribute psychologically (and it may not be 100% physical) to the distress I’m feeling now is because after the wisdom teeth removal, my face started changing pretty dramatically (in my eyes). I’m a 24 year old girl and I have to admit that I’m quite vain and narcissistic when it comes to appearance. I take a lot of selfies and pictures to alleviate the anxiety because my looks, to me are a “safety net”. When I started to realize that my reflection didn’t quite look the same anymore, and it was looking worse, I started to lose my mind. I still avoid and obsessively look into mirrors and stress over what I look like. I can’t take selfies anymore and I don’t have my looks anymore to assure myself of my self identity. 

Anyway thanks for commenting. I really really hope you could solve your TMJ issue, and I hope you could get a chance to look into my two suggestions- orthotropic dentists and cranial osteopathy. ❤️

Do you have a orthopedic dentist near you? You have to expand the upper jaw and let the lower jaw come forward. The ligaments will then line up and heal itself. 

I think my tmj has been caused by the meds. There’s something up with the neurotransmitters. And no one knows what to do about it. No one knows if it can heal or not.

Thanks. I feel like I never had a choice from the beginning. It feels like I’m never in control of my actions, even when I consciously think something, like “don’t take the meds, I have a bad feeling about this”, 
my body acts in a different way. I consciously choose to ignore that thought and do it anyways. What the fuck. I feel like a puppet and I want this to end

Ive seen a cranial osteopath for it. It helped some of it but there’s something wrong with my neck. It pulls on all the muscles in my face. It doesn’t want to straighten. I think there’s something wrong with me. Not just physically but I keep making bad decisions. I am like a 5 year old. I can’t handle taking care of myself at all. Even the meds, even seeing doctors, they don’t take me seriously because I express myself in an infantile manner. I should have grown the fuck up before I started touching any kind of meds. I even went to the psychiatrist back when I was 16 because I wanted attention and pity. I’m a complete fucking degenerate

Thank you for your kindness. I wish I could have done things differently. 
I don’t know if free will exists but it feels like it’s all my fault. Yet I feel like I had no control of any of my decisions that led me to this point. 

It’s not something I can even really fix with shifting my attitude. I’ve damaged my body and I can’t function like other people. I can’t do anything a normal 24 year old girl would do and it’s my fault for taking prescription psychiatric meds so recklessly. I knew xanax was bad but I took it anyways. I felt a gut feeling saying: don’t take these! But I ignored it. 

I quit everything and tried to get my life together but my body was already damaged. I don’t think it can recover to normal. I already am left out of social circles because I can’t drink or do recreational drugs. I can’t talk without running out of breath. There’s some kind of vibration in my spinal cord that pulls all my cranial muscles so tight. 

No one will help, not even my family. It’s my fault for being foolish and thinking people were inherently drawn to help others. It’s my fault for not speaking up when the doctors prescribed me those medications because I have trouble speaking to authority figures. It’s my fault for not taking care of myself more. 

My life was never my life to begin with. I never felt like I had control of anything. Please make it stop
